prompts.spl: `sap_logserv_idx_macro` (sourcetype="sap:hana:audit" OR sourcetype="sap:sapstartsrv") action_category="Authentication" earliest=-30d@h latest=now | eval auth_user = coalesce(executing_user, user) | where isnotnull(auth_user) | bin _time span=1h | stats count by auth_user, _time | eventstats avg(count) AS avg_count, stdev(count) AS stdev_count by auth_user | eval z_score = round((count - avg_count) / stdev_count, 2) | where _time >= relative_time(now(), "-1d@d") AND z_score > 3 AND count > 10 | sort -z_score

prompts.label: Anomaly: webdispatcher response time
prompts.description: Per-host web-dispatcher average-latency Z-score against a 30-day baseline, read from the hourly web-timing rollup. Runs daily and detects hours of the most recent day where a host's response time deviated sharply from its own historical pattern.
prompts.interpretation: Each row is a host whose average response time in an hour of the most recent day is statistically anomalous (max_rt shows the worst single request that hour). Investigate backend health, network path, or cache state. Combined with the avg_rt > 200ms floor, this filters out noisy alerts on consistently fast hosts.

nextSteps.text: Pull the per-URI breakdown for the slow hour to see which endpoints dominate.
nextSteps.spl: `sap_logserv_idx_macro` sourcetype="sap:webdispatcher:access" host="<host>" earliest=-1h@h latest=now | stats avg(response_time_ms) AS avg_rt, perc95(response_time_ms) AS p95_rt, count by uri | sort -p95_rt

nextSteps: Cross-check with edge-data Performance tab on the topology view for the same host to see whether RFC / HANA tenant latency is also elevated (system-wide degradation vs. webdispatcher-specific).
Check infrastructure dashboards (CPU, memory, network) for the host during the anomalous window.
prompts.spl: | inputlookup logserv_web_timing_rollup where metric="wd_host" | where bucket_ts>=relative_time(now(), "-30d@h") AND host!="(none)" | eval avg_rt=round(if(cnt_rt>0, sum_rt/cnt_rt, 0), 1), _time=bucket_ts | eventstats avg(avg_rt) AS baseline_avg, stdev(avg_rt) AS stdev_avg by host | eval z_score = round((avg_rt - baseline_avg) / stdev_avg, 2) | where _time >= relative_time(now(), "-1d@d") AND z_score > 3 AND avg_rt > 200 | table _time host count avg_rt max_rt baseline_avg stdev_avg z_score | sort -z_score

prompts.label: Anomaly: topology edge call volume
prompts.description: Reads pre-aggregated edge bucket rows from the logserv_topology_edges KV Store. Runs daily and detects edges whose call_count in any hour of the most recent day is statistically anomalous vs. that edge's own 30-day baseline.
prompts.interpretation: Each row is a topology edge (source to target, with type) whose hourly call volume on the most recent day deviates from its own historical pattern. Surge = surge in cross-system traffic (could be brute-force or a surge in legitimate workload); drop = integration outage. The Z-score sign tells you which direction. Reads from KV Store, no live SPL on raw indexes.
nextSteps: For surge anomalies (positive Z), check whether the source system is making more requests than usual or whether the target is being targeted.
For drop anomalies (negative Z), confirm the source service is healthy on its own dashboards before declaring an integration outage.
Open the Environment Topology view, click the anomalous edge, and review the Activity tab for the historical trend visualization.
prompts.spl: | inputlookup logserv_topology_edges | where bucket_ts >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@h") | eventstats avg(call_count) AS baseline_avg, stdev(call_count) AS baseline_stdev by source, target, type | where bucket_ts >= relative_time(now(), "-1d@d") | eval z_score = round((call_count - baseline_avg) / baseline_stdev, 2) | where abs(z_score) > 3 AND call_count > 10 | sort -z_score

prompts.label: Anomaly: per-admin off-hours activity
prompts.description: Per-admin off-hours activity baseline vs. that admin's 30-day off-hours pattern. Z-score threshold lower (>2) than other anomaly searches because admin off-hours activity is naturally rare and low absolute counts can still be anomalous.
prompts.interpretation: Each row is an admin user whose yesterday-off-hours activity exceeds their own 30-day off-hours baseline. Healthy environments show 0-1 rows during normal weeks; planned weekend cutovers will produce hits that should map to documented change tickets.

nextSteps.text: Pull the full off-hours activity for the admin to see exactly what happened.
nextSteps.spl: `sap_logserv_idx_macro` sourcetype="sap:hana:audit" is_admin_user="true" is_business_hours="false" (executing_user="<user>" OR user="<user>") earliest=-2d@d latest=now | sort 0 _time | table _time host action_category action_type target_user _raw

nextSteps: Confirm the activity maps to a change ticket; off-hours admin activity without a ticket is the canonical "after-hours admin compromise" indicator.

nextSteps.text: Cross-check with after_hours_admin_data_access to see if the admin was active in the webdispatcher tier as well.

prompts.spl: `sap_logserv_idx_macro` sourcetype="sap:hana:audit" is_admin_user="true" earliest=-30d@d latest=now | eval auth_user = coalesce(executing_user, user), oh_hour = tonumber(strftime(_time, "%H")) | where isnotnull(auth_user) AND (oh_hour < 8 OR oh_hour >= 18) | bin _time span=1d | stats count by auth_user, _time | eventstats avg(count) AS daily_avg, stdev(count) AS daily_stdev by auth_user | eval z_score = round((count - daily_avg) / daily_stdev, 2) | where _time >= relative_time(now(), "-1d@d") AND z_score > 2 AND count > 5 | sort -z_score
